notes.milestones: Row id or `prefix*` to the milestone of docs/plans/rca-parity/plan.md section 6 in which the row becomes served; the longest match wins. aiVault.* and orchestration.party* stay pending until decision 1 (by M7); pairing.* until decision 1 (by M5).
notes.reverify: Row id to why a trace hit does not serve it yet: the host answers without doing the work. A call that only passes by refusing or by an empty answer never counts; remove the note in the commit that makes the answer functional and reverified through the chain.
notes.traceNoise: Row id or `prefix*` to why a trace may name a row the phone does not reach (the crawl drives the whole host surface): `wf mimic coverage --traces` does not report such a row as unknown-trace-row. A row the phone reaches never needs one, and a mistyped row a test names is not noise.
notes.unrecordable: A served row no recording can show (a pty's output, a restart, a clock, an interaction no recorded set holds): a row decision with an `unrecordable` reason, or the top-level `unrecordableTests` map of `file::test` (or `file::*`) to the reason; `wf mimic coverage --by-oracle` classes it (d). A served row with neither `"oracle": "mimic"` nor this reason fails `wf mimic coverage --check` (rule served-without-oracle).
notes.decisions: Rows with a state other than pending: not-offered needs a reason and a decidedBy milestone, excluded a reason. Flagged (ORCA_SIDEBAR_INPUTS_IS_MAIN) and off-allowlist rows are classed by the scan itself. No row is marked served here: served needs run-bundle evidence. A row may carry `"oracle": "mimic"` (docs/plans/mimic/plan.md): only a `wf mimic replay --suite` trace whose call is labelled clean or allowlisted on a `recorded` cassette serves it, never a behaviour test.
notes.knownGapReasons: Why a recorded case stays a listed breaking gap instead of being fixed: rpc:ui.set (crawl ids orca-ui.set-valid-min and orca-ui.set-boundary-full, `ui.jiraSavedFilterState` missing): the crawl sets it with ui.mutateJiraSavedFilters, a method the phone never calls (orca-methods.json: phone false, allowlist execution-host). The table test `every_served_method_is_a_phone_row...` is kept without an exception list: a served non-phone row would let the table claim methods nothing in the product reaches, and the exception would be this one row's. Serving the method only to replay one crawl field is not parity of anything the phone does, so the two cases stay gap-listed (breaking) until the crawl stops depending on the order of a desktop-only write.

unrecordableTests.terminal_pty::a_phone_streams_a_real_she: a pty's output: the headless orcad has no open app window and answers every terminal row with that refusal, so no recording holds the bytes a shell prints, what typed input runs, a resumed stream or a resize; the recorded replay serves the rows and this test keeps the pty check

traceNoise.rpc:layout.*: the desktop window's workspace layout (apply, snapshots, held panes, view reports, subscribe): the scan finds no phone caller, and the recorded crawl drives the host's whole method surface, so its trace names them without a phone row to serve
traceNoise.rpc:sidebarInputs.*: the desktop sidebar's inputs (activity, desktop and review facts, paired server rows, workspace rows and creations, temporal, report view): no phone caller in the scan; the crawl names them, and the two phone rows (read, repoIcons) are flagged rows the scan classes itself
traceNoise.rpc:sidebarSession.begin: opens the desktop sidebar's input session: no phone caller in the scan, named by the crawl alone
traceNoise.rpc:session.readTerminalScrollback: reads a terminal's scrollback for the desktop's execution host: no phone caller in the scan (the phone reads a terminal through terminal.subscribe, a pending M8 row), named by the crawl alone
